Breakfast.

Meet your English-speaking guide in the hotel lobby at the arranged time and transfer to the railway station. Take the train to Aguas Calientes, a small town at the foot of Machu Picchu also known as Machu Picchu Pueblo.

The highlight of the day is a guided visit to Machu Picchu, the legendary ‘Lost City of the Incas’ and one of the world's most striking archaeological sites.

Machu Picchu means ‘Old Mountain’ in Quechua. The ancient city was built in the 15th century on a remote ridge in the Andes, with sweeping views of green slopes and deep valleys. Its isolated location helped it survive the destruction that befell many other Inca settlements during the Spanish conquest.

Machu Picchu became widely known in 1911 through the work of American explorer Hiram Bingham. Local people had known about it long before his expedition.

On your visit, you'll learn about the history of the ancient city and see stone terraces, ceremonial plazas, temples and other structures that show the skill of Inca engineers and builders.

Machu Picchu became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1983 and was named one of the New Seven Wonders of the World in 2007.

Lunch at a restaurant.

After the guided visit, return to the railway station for the train back to Cusco. Transfer to your hotel on arrival.

Overnight at the 4-star Xima Cusco or a similar hotel in the same category.

Breakfast.

Spend the day exploring Cusco at your own pace. Wander its narrow streets, visit museums and souvenir shops, or stop at a café.

Optional excursions are available if you'd like to see more of Peru.
